about.title: Monterey Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a traffic collision takes a life in Monterey, the loss ripples through a family in ways that are hard to put into words. Monterey County sees hundreds of injury collisions each year, and while most people walk away hurt but alive, some do not. If you've lost a spouse, parent, child, or someone who depended on you financially, California law gives certain family members and dependents the right to bring a wrongful death claim. This is separate from any criminal case that might follow a fatal crash, and it exists to help surviving family members recover some measure of stability after an unimaginable loss. LawProactive connects grieving families in Monterey with an independent attorney who can walk through what happened, who may have standing to file, and what the timeline looks like. You don't have to sort through this alone, and there's no upfront cost to start the conversation.

items.title: Who Can File Matters
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain other dependents or heirs. An attorney can help sort out who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity was involved, such as a city road or municipal vehicle. Waiting too long can close the door on a claim entirely.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, but also compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance the person provided. An attorney can help explain how these losses are documented and valued.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation and explain who qualifies to bring the claim.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing a loved one in a Monterey crash?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the crash involved a government vehicle or a road maintained by a public entity, that deadline can be much shorter. It's worth speaking with an attorney early so you don't lose the ability to file.

items.question: Does it matter that this happened on a road like Highway 68 or Del Monte Avenue?
items.answer: Monterey's higher-traffic corridors, including Del Monte Avenue, Lighthouse Avenue, Highway 68, and Fremont Street, see a larger share of reported collisions, which can affect how evidence like traffic reports or camera footage is gathered. An attorney familiar with local roads can help piece together what happened. This doesn't change your legal rights, but it can shape how the claim is investigated.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, these are separate processes. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil case brought by the family seeking compensation for their losses. You can pursue a civil claim regardless of what happens, or doesn't happen, in criminal court.
